sections.title: Setup
sections.text: Two players use 40-card decks with at least six base creatures. At most three copies of a card ID, except Energy which is unlimited. A seeded shuffle is followed by moving the first base creature to the active slot, then drawing seven cards. This guaranteed-companion setup replaces mulligans. You begin; first player cannot attack on turn one. There is one active creature and three reserve slots per player. No prizes are removed from the deck.

sections.title: Turns
sections.text: Draw one at the start of each turn, except the first turn. Deploy base creatures, evolve, use abilities, attach one energy, play at most one Guide, equip Tools, and retreat at most once in any order. Attack once to end your turn, or End turn without attacking. Cards and abilities resolve atomically with no response stack. There is no hand size limit.

sections.title: Evolution
sections.text: Each family has a base plus four evolutions, stages 0-4. Evolve onto the previous stage of the same family; field-record variants count as the same form. The creature must have been in play since a previous own turn. It cannot evolve on your first turn or twice during the same own turn. Keep its damage amount, energy, Tool and evolution stack. Clear toxin. Higher maximum health does not erase existing damage.

sections.title: Energy and Retreat
sections.text: Pay matching requirements before generic ones. Any energy pays generic; only the printed element pays matching requirements. Energy stays attached after attacking unless an extra discard is specified. Extra energy discards remove the first attached energy in attachment order. Retreat discards the printed number of energies, switches with a chosen reserve, and clears toxin on the outgoing creature. Switch Guides cost no energy and do not consume your once-per-turn retreat. A Tool slot accepts only one Tool until the creature is knocked out.

sections.title: Damage and Conditions
sections.text: Base attack plus Tool bonus is increased by 20 for defender weakness, or decreased by 20 for resistance, then reduced by armor and the one-hit shield (minimum zero). Weakness/resistance use attacker element. A shield is consumed by the next direct attack even if damage is zero. Toxin causes 10 damage at the end of its owner turn, including turns without attacks. Toxin does not stack; shields and armor do not prevent toxin or recoil. Signature effects resolve after direct damage and before knockout checks. Siphons do not exist; self-heal restores 10. Recoil deals 10 to the attacker. Draw effects may cause fatigue before the knockout batch.

sections.title: Abilities and Guides
sections.text: Stage 2-4 creatures have one once-per-own-turn ability: nurture heals self 10, ward sets a 10 shield, insight draws one. Newly evolved creatures may use their ability if that creature has not already used one this turn. Bench abilities work. Guides invoke effects.json operations for healing, draw, searching, switching, disruption, recovery, shields and cleansing. Tools provide passive attack or armor bonuses. Searches choose a matching card ID from your own deck and shuffle afterward. Illegal targets or costs change no state.

sections.title: Knockouts and Victory
sections.text: Knockouts are collected simultaneously after the full action and its effects. Discard the entire creature stack, all energy and its Tool. The opponent earns one crest, or two for a stage 3-4 knockout. Reach four crests, or leave the opponent without any creature in play, to win. If both qualify in the same check, draw. A knockout with reserves asks that owner to promote one; promotions happen before the next turn begins. A basic in hand or deck does not prevent defeat when no creature remains in play.

sections.title: Deck Exhaustion and Limits
sections.text: Each failed draw deals escalating fatigue to the active creature: 10 on the first, 20 on the second, and so on. After turn 100, compare 100 times crests plus remaining creature health plus five times attached energy; equal scores draw. This guarantees a finite match. No collectible purchases, real money, multiplayer, or commercial game data are included.

sections.title: Library and Rights
sections.text: 150 original families have 750 named forms (base plus four evolutions). The complete catalog has 17,825 creature printings, 2,863 Guide/Tool printings and 568 Energy printings: 21,256 total. Expansion field records share mechanics with the foundation; they are not 21,256 independently designed or balanced cards. 150 local generated family illustrations are shared across evolution stages with tinting, not 750 separate paintings. No affiliation with any commercial creature-card game is claimed. Source and component licenses are available locally.
